easy.q: What is the first book of the Bible?
easy.p: Genesis is Greek for 'origin'; its Hebrew title 'Bereshit' means 'in the beginning.'

easy.q: What is the last book of the Bible?
easy.p: 'Revelation' translates the Greek 'apokalypsis' — an unveiling.

easy.q: Who built the ark?
easy.p: The ark was longer than a football field by the cubits given.

easy.q: Where was Jesus born?
easy.p: 'Bethlehem' means 'house of bread' — fitting for the Bread of Life.

easy.q: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
easy.p: Jonah is the only prophet who fled the opposite way from his call.

easy.q: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
easy.p: Twelve disciples echo Israel's twelve tribes — a new people forming.

easy.q: Who betrayed Jesus?
easy.p: Thirty pieces of silver was the price of a slave in Exodus 21:32.

easy.q: Who baptized Jesus?
easy.p: John and Jesus were kin — Elizabeth and Mary were relatives.

easy.q: Who was the mother of Jesus?
easy.p: Mary was likely still a teenager when Gabriel appeared to her.

easy.q: Who denied Jesus three times?
easy.p: A rooster's crow still marks Peter's threefold denial.

easy.q: Who was the first man?
easy.p: 'Adam' is Hebrew for 'man,' from 'adamah,' the ground he was formed from.

easy.q: Who was the first woman?
easy.p: 'Eve' means 'living' — the mother of all the living.

easy.q: What did Jesus turn water into?
easy.p: Water into wine at Cana was Jesus' first recorded miracle.

easy.q: Who killed Goliath?
easy.p: David felled Goliath with a sling — an ordinary shepherd's tool.

easy.q: "The Lord is my ___" (Psalm 23)
easy.p: Psalm 23 is the best-loved psalm, penned by David the shepherd-king.

easy.q: What sign did God give Noah after the flood?
easy.p: The rainbow sealed God's promise never again to flood the earth.

easy.q: On which day did God rest?
easy.p: The weekly Sabbath is rooted here, in creation's seventh day.

easy.q: Who led Israel out of Egypt?
easy.p: Moses' name may mean 'drawn out' — of the water he was pulled from.

easy.q: Who was thrown into the lions' den?
easy.p: Daniel served under the empires of both Babylon and Persia.

easy.q: What did Jesus ride into Jerusalem?
easy.p: Riding a donkey signalled peace; a warhorse would signal conquest.

easy.q: How many days did it rain in the flood?
easy.p: Forty is Scripture's recurring number for testing and preparation.

easy.q: What was the garden where Adam and Eve lived?
easy.p: 'Eden' means 'delight' — a garden God planted Himself.

med.q: How many books are in the Protestant Bible?
med.p: 'Bible' comes from the Greek 'biblia' — simply 'the books.'

med.q: How many plagues struck Egypt?
med.p: The tenth plague, the firstborn, gave rise to the Passover.

med.q: Which sea did Moses part?
med.p: The Hebrew 'Yam Suph' can also be read 'Sea of Reeds.'

med.q: On which mountain were the Ten Commandments given?
med.p: Sinai is also called Horeb, 'the mountain of God.'

med.q: Who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams?
med.p: Joseph rose from a prison cell to Egypt's second-in-command.

med.q: Who was the wisest king of Israel?
med.p: Solomon asked God for wisdom over riches — and received both.

med.q: Who was the first king of Israel?
med.p: Saul stood a head taller than anyone else in Israel.

med.q: Whose strength left him when his hair was cut?
med.p: Samson was a Nazirite; his uncut hair marked a vow, not magic.

med.q: Which prophet was taken up in a whirlwind?
med.p: Elijah never died — he was taken up in a chariot of fire.

med.q: Which apostle had been a tax collector?
med.p: Tax collectors were despised as collaborators with Rome.

med.q: Where were believers first called "Christians"?
med.p: Antioch, in modern Turkey, became the early church's mission base.

med.q: Who wrote most of the New Testament letters?
med.p: Paul is credited with roughly 13 of the New Testament's 27 books.

med.q: On the road to where was Saul converted?
med.p: Damascus is among the world's oldest continuously lived-in cities.

med.q: Who climbed a tree to see Jesus?
med.p: Zacchaeus was a wealthy chief tax collector, widely resented.

med.q: How many people were saved on Noah's ark?
med.p: Only eight people — Noah's family — survived the flood.

med.q: How many loaves fed the five thousand?
med.p: Feeding the 5,000 is the sole miracle in all four Gospels.

med.q: Which disciple doubted the resurrection?
med.p: 'Doubting Thomas' became shorthand for a hard-nosed sceptic.

med.q: Which queen saved her people from Haman?
med.p: Esther and Ruth are the only Bible books named for women.

med.q: How many days was Lazarus dead before being raised?
med.p: Four days dead meant, to onlookers, all hope was gone.

med.q: What food did God provide in the wilderness?
med.p: 'Manna' comes from the Hebrew for 'What is it?'

med.q: Who was renamed from Abram?
med.p: 'Abram' means 'exalted father'; 'Abraham,' 'father of many.'

med.q: What was Abraham's promised son's name?
med.p: 'Isaac' means 'he laughs' — Sarah laughed at the promise.

med.q: Who walked on water then began to sink?
med.p: 'Peter' means 'rock'; Jesus renamed him from Simon.

med.q: Who was Ruth's mother-in-law?
med.p: Naomi renamed herself 'Mara' — 'bitter' — in her grief.

med.q: Who tried to wash his hands of Jesus' death?
med.p: Pilate governed Judea about ten years for Rome.

hard.q: What is the shortest verse in the Bible (KJV)?
hard.p: At two words, John 11:35 is the shortest verse in English Bibles.

hard.q: What was Paul's trade?
hard.p: Paul funded his own missionary journeys by making tents.

hard.q: Which three were thrown into the fiery furnace?
hard.p: Their Babylonian names replaced Hebrew ones that honoured God.

hard.q: Which book has the most chapters?
hard.p: Psalms holds 150 chapters — plus the Bible's longest and shortest.

hard.q: Who was the first Christian martyr?
hard.p: Saul, later Paul, stood approving as Stephen was stoned.

hard.q: How many fruits of the Spirit are listed (Gal 5)?
hard.p: One fruit of the Spirit, nine facets — and love leads them.

hard.q: Who is called "a man after God's own heart"?
hard.p: David is the Bible's most-named human after Jesus Himself.

hard.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
hard.p: The dove's olive leaf became a lasting emblem of peace.

hard.q: Who succeeded Moses to lead Israel?
hard.p: 'Joshua' is the Hebrew form of 'Jesus' — 'the Lord saves.'

hard.q: How many books are in the Old Testament?
hard.p: The 39 Old Testament books were written mostly in Hebrew.

hard.q: Which prophet was told to marry Gomer?
hard.p: Hosea's marriage dramatised God's love for a wayward Israel.

hard.q: Who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls as governor?
hard.p: Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem's walls in just 52 days.

hard.q: In which garden did Jesus pray before His arrest?
hard.p: 'Gethsemane' means 'oil press' — an olive grove near Jerusalem.

hard.q: Whose ear did Peter cut off at Jesus' arrest?
hard.p: Luke the physician alone notes Jesus healed the severed ear.

hard.q: Who was the father of John the Baptist?
hard.p: Zechariah was struck mute until John was born and named.

hard.q: How many years did the Israelites wander in the wilderness?
hard.p: One year of wandering for each day the spies scouted Canaan.

hard.q: Which Gospel was written by a physician?
hard.p: Luke wrote more of the New Testament by volume than anyone.

hard.q: What was the name of Abraham's wife?
hard.p: Sarah bore Isaac at 90; her name means 'princess.'

hard.q: In what city was Paul imprisoned when he wrote several epistles?
hard.p: His 'prison letters' include Ephesians, Philippians and Colossians.

hard.q: Who was the oldest man recorded in the Bible?
hard.p: Methuselah's 969 years is the longest lifespan in Scripture.

edifying.q: According to Philippians 4:6-7, what guards our hearts when we pray with thanksgiving instead of worrying?
edifying.n: The peace of God, beyond understanding, guards your heart and mind.
edifying.r: Philippians 4:6-7 — bring it to God before you carry it alone.
edifying.p: Paul wrote Philippians from prison — yet its theme is joy.

edifying.q: What did Jesus call the greatest commandment?
o: Love the Lord your God with all your heart
edifying.n: Love God fully — and your neighbour as yourself.
edifying.p: Jesus drew this from Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18.

edifying.q: According to Micah 6:8, what does the Lord require of us?
o: Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly
edifying.n: Justice, mercy, and humility before God.
edifying.r: Micah 6:8 — a whole life in one verse.
edifying.p: Many call this one verse the heart of the prophets' message.

edifying.q: In Galatians 5, the fruit of the Spirit begins with which quality?
edifying.n: Love — then joy, peace, patience, and the rest.
edifying.p: Nine qualities, one fruit — grown by the Spirit, not willpower.

edifying.q: Proverbs 3:5 tells us to trust in the Lord and not lean on our own ___.
edifying.n: Trust Him fully; He makes your paths straight.
edifying.p: Proverbs pairs trusting God with releasing our need to figure it out.

edifying.q: According to Romans 12:2, we are transformed by the renewing of our ___.
edifying.n: A renewed mind reshapes how you live.
edifying.p: 'Transformed' here is the Greek 'metamorphoo' — a full change.

edifying.q: Matthew 6:33 says to seek first the ___ of God.
edifying.n: Seek His kingdom first; the rest is added.
edifying.p: From the Sermon on the Mount — seek first, and worry loosens.

edifying.q: According to John 13:35, how will everyone know we are Jesus' disciples?
o: By our love for one another
edifying.n: Love is the mark of a disciple.
edifying.p: Jesus said this the very night before the cross.

edifying.q: James 1:19 says to be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to ___.
edifying.n: Listen first; anger last.
edifying.p: James is the New Testament's most practical, proverb-like letter.

edifying.q: Psalm 119:105 calls God's word a lamp to my feet and a ___ to my path.
edifying.n: The Word lights the next step.
edifying.p: Psalm 119, the Bible's longest chapter, is all about God's Word.

edifying.q: In 1 Corinthians 13, which remains the greatest?
edifying.n: Faith, hope and love remain — the greatest is love.
edifying.p: Read at countless weddings — but written to a divided church.

edifying.q: Ephesians 2:8-9 says we are saved by grace through ___, not by works.
edifying.n: Grace is a gift, never a wage.
edifying.p: Grace plus nothing — the verse at the Reformation's core.

edifying.q: Isaiah 40:31 says those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength and soar on wings like ___.
edifying.n: Wait on Him and rise renewed.
edifying.p: Isaiah wrote this to exiles who felt completely worn out.

edifying.q: In the Beatitudes, the peacemakers are called the ___ of God.
edifying.n: Blessed are the peacemakers.
edifying.p: The Beatitudes open Jesus' Sermon on the Mount.

edifying.q: Joshua 1:9 commands us to be strong and ___, for the Lord is with us.
edifying.n: Courage flows from His presence.
edifying.p: God said this as Joshua stepped into Moses' shoes.

edifying.q: Romans 8:28 says all things work together for ___ to those who love God.
edifying.n: Even hard things are woven for good.
edifying.p: Romans 8 ends: nothing can separate us from God's love.

edifying.q: Matthew 11:28 — "Come to me, all you who are weary, and I will give you ___."
edifying.n: Bring the weight to Him; receive rest.
edifying.p: The image is a shared yoke — rest carried together, not alone.

edifying.q: 2 Timothy 1:7 — God gave us a spirit not of fear, but of power, love and a sound ___.
edifying.n: Power, love, self-discipline — not fear.
edifying.p: Paul wrote this final letter to young Timothy near his death.

edifying.q: Hebrews 11:1 — faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not ___.
edifying.n: Faith sees what eyes cannot yet.
edifying.p: Hebrews 11 then parades the great 'heroes of faith.'

edifying.q: 1 John 1:9 — if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to ___ us.
edifying.n: Confession meets faithful forgiveness.
edifying.p: 'Faithful and just' — forgiveness is God keeping His own word.

edifying.q: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 — rejoice always, pray continually, and give ___ in all circumstances.
edifying.n: Gratitude in everything is God's will for you.
edifying.p: Three brief commands Paul calls simply 'God's will for you.'

edifying.q: Psalm 46:10 — "Be still, and know that I am ___."
edifying.n: Stillness is where we know Him.
edifying.p: 'Be still' renders a Hebrew word meaning 'let go, cease striving.'

edifying.q: Galatians 6:9 — let us not grow weary in doing ___, for we will reap a harvest.
edifying.n: Keep sowing good; the harvest comes.
edifying.p: Paul's farming image: sow now, reap in God's timing.

edifying.q: Romans 5:8 — while we were still ___, Christ died for us.
edifying.n: Loved before we deserved it.
edifying.p: The gospel in a line — loved before we ever turned back.

edifying.q: Colossians 3:23 — whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the ___.
edifying.n: Ordinary work becomes worship.
edifying.p: Written for slaves and workers: all labour can honour God.

edifying.q: Matthew 6:14 — if you forgive others, your heavenly Father will also ___ you.
edifying.n: Forgiveness given opens forgiveness received.
edifying.p: This follows immediately after the Lord's Prayer.

edifying.q: Philippians 4:13 — "I can do all things through ___ who strengthens me."
edifying.n: Strength for all things is found in Him.
edifying.p: Often quoted for success; Paul meant contentment in any lot.

edifying.q: Proverbs 17:17 — a ___ loves at all times.
edifying.n: Steady love marks true friendship.
edifying.p: Its partner line: 'a brother is born for adversity.'

edifying.q: John 14:6 — Jesus said, "I am the way, the ___, and the life."
edifying.n: The way, the truth, the life.
edifying.p: One of John's seven great 'I am' sayings.

edifying.q: Lamentations 3:23 — His mercies are new every ___.
edifying.n: Fresh mercy waits each morning.
edifying.p: Lamentations mourns Jerusalem's fall — yet hope breaks through.
